records.content: WFXRtv Measles outbreak in Central Virginia officially over, VDH declares Dawn Forrest 2 days ago (WFXR) – After 154 cases in just over three months, the measles outbreak in Buckingham County is officially over, the Virginia Department of Health (VDH) revealed. Over 42 days must pass after a recorded infection for VDH administrators to formally end an outbreak. The most recent outbreak-related case was confirmed June 29, meeting that requirement. It’s a triumphant end to a regional health emergency, VDH officials said, but they’re not letting their guard down just yet. Places where less than 95% of the population are MMR-vaccinated are more vulnerable to measles outbreaks. In Buckingham County, that rate is just above 74%. It’s even lower in neighboring Cumberland County at around 65%. While local health departments will continue respond to suspected cases, there could be people infected who do not report the disease. Health officials said it’s a good reminder to get vaccinated, especially as parents are sending their kids back to school. “I think my colleagues and I to be transparent and clear about the benefits and potential risks of different strategies like vaccination,” said Dr. Lauri Forlano, VDH state epidemiologist. “But overwhelmingly, the risk-benefit profile is in favor of being vaccinated.” People can check their MMR vaccination status here. Those two different exposures are at; Millersville University (August 4-5): Individuals attending a soccer camp at Millersville University on August 4 and 5 may have been exposed. Camp attendees are being notified of the potential exposure and provided with resources. Whole Foods Market (August 12): Individuals visiting the Whole Foods Market at 1563 Fruitville Pike, Lancaster, PA 17601 on August 12, may have been exposed to measles. DOH advises anyone who may have been exposed to check their vaccination status and monitor for symptoms. Individuals who are not vaccinated are most at-risk for infection. Getting vaccinated is the best protection from the highly contagious measles virus, providing 97% lifetime protection after two doses. DOH instructed the individuals who tested positive to isolate at home while contagious. For privacy reasons, the Department cannot provide details about the individuals. Measles is a highly contagious virus that infects the lungs and spreads when an infected person breaths, coughs, or sneezes. The virus remains in the air and on surfaces for up to two hours, even after the infected person leaves the area. Symptoms to watch for include fever, cough, runny nose, and red, watery eyes, followed by a rash that starts on the head or face and spreads downward. Symptoms can start 7 to 21 days after exposure. The only way to prevent measles is with the MMR vaccine. People who believe they were exposed to measles, and are experiencing symptoms, should contact their health care provider or call the Department’s toll-free hotline at 877-PA-HEALTH (877-724-3258).
